title: Espresso Dial-In Drift by Bean Age
dataSources: Sourdough monitor (`sourdough:reading`), BBQ/sous-vide probes (`bbq:probe`), fridge/freezer/oven temperature (`kitchen:appliance`), espresso shots (`espresso:shot`), pantry inventory (`pantry:item`), kombucha brew (`kombucha:reading`).
app: ESP32/ESPHome kitchen sensors (sourdough rise, BBQ/sous-vide probes, fridge/freezer temperature), espresso-shot logs, and pantry inventory via MQTT and Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=espresso:shot
| stats avg(shot_time_s) as avg_time, avg(yield_g) as avg_yield by bean_name bean_age_days
| where bean_age_days>21 AND (avg_time<22 OR avg_time>35)
| sort bean_age_days
description: Shows how extraction behaviour shifts as beans age, helping you notice when the grind or dose drift is really a freshness drift.
value: Dial-in consistency is easier when freshness is part of the picture; this query links shot behaviour to bean age explicitly.
implementation: Forward espresso shot logs with bean age metadata; review older beans that are drifting outside your normal extraction window.
visualization: Scatter plot of bean age versus average shot time.
grandmaExplanation: It ranks how the age of your coffee beans is starting to change the way your espresso shots pull.
